definition: An ORM scores only the final answer; a PRM scores each intermediate reasoning step.
details: An ORM scores only the final answer; a PRM scores each intermediate reasoning step. PRMs give denser signal and better-guided search but are expensive to label and can be gamed by plausible-looking steps.

explainer.lead: An ORM scores only the final answer from a reasoning model, whereas a PRM scores each intermediate reasoning step. The distinction matters because it changes how much guidance a model gets and at what cost.

tiers.eli5: One judge only looks at the last line of your homework; the other checks every step along the way.
tiers.practitioner: PRMs give denser signal and better-guided search but are expensive to label and can be gamed by plausible-looking steps. A pitfall is trusting step scores that reward steps that merely look reasonable.
tiers.paperLevel: An ORM scores only the final answer; a PRM scores each intermediate reasoning step. PRMs offer denser signal and better-guided search, at the cost of expensive labelling and susceptibility to gaming by plausible-looking steps.

explainer.example: For a maths problem, an ORM grades just the submitted answer, while a PRM grades every line of the derivation before the answer.
